page.layout: One page of text in running prose, with a centred closing prayer at its foot. Marginal notes in the right margin. Below the text a printed fleuron (ornament), then the signature at the foot.

main_text.p: libertatem philosophicam amant, eâq; veluti clypeo muniti, ingrediuntur silvam philosophicam in primo limine, in quo varia lustra, fera indomita, & aves rapaces, tenebricosam; sed in penetra[illegible, ~1 letter]bus clarissimam, ubi animalia amicabilia, arbores elegantula, fructus dulces, avicula dulcisonæ, flosculi suaveolentes visuntur. Libertas philoso-phica quid sit? Adeste ergo, qui satagitis pugnare contra Tria mon-stra, contra quaedimicare debet literarum alumnus. monstra illa IGNORANTIAM, FALSITATEM, CONFUSIONEM, quæ oberrant in hac, quam dixi silvâ, & oppressum eunt SCIENTIAM, VERITATEM, ORDINEM. Adeste, inquam, & hoc filo Tres literarum & literatorum fores. Ariadneo utimini in cæco illo labyrintho. Pau-cis enim vobis ostendam rectam cynosuram & manuductionem, quam secuti non aberrabitis, ut est in proverbio, à janua. Tu vero, Domine Deus, pater cœlestis, da mihi recta scribere, tibi in honorem, aliis in fructum.

page.notes: Printed fleuron (ornament) below the text, not transcribed. The Greek-free text has no doubtful words except the following. "eâq;" is printed with a small superscript mark after the q that I could not read with certainty; it is copied as "eâq;" and should be checked. The word in "penetra..bus" has a damaged letter where a single letter (probably l) should be; it is marked illegible. The note "quaedimicare" is printed with a hyphen split as "quaedimica-re" and is copied whole. Long s in the notes ("monstra") is written as plain s. The printed "ut est" is copied as "ut est". Running head and page number are printed at the top. Signature "A 2" is at the foot.
